text:
deploybot: pin applied -> runtime/runtime-3.2.1 added to pinlist for scope=canary-eu-west. reason=kv-cache growth causing OOMs. auto-notify oncall. link: https://deploy.internal/pins/4690123456 :warning:
kevin: ugh. what triggered it? is this traffic-specific or a kernel regression?
tara: quick summary — canary saw kv-cache resident size spike ~3.4% of requests (baseline ~0.8%). correlates with longseq LLM requests + quantized path. heap growth, then oom. stack traces point to new kernel change in 3.2.1 (kv eviction path).
jamie: thanks. can we soft-pin (serve degraded) vs hard-block? we usually prefer soft to avoid customer impact. what does deploybot do here?
deploybot: soft-pin enacted by default for this automation. behavior: route new canary requests to fallback runtime-3.1.x while honoring existing sessions for 3.2.1 for up to 5m. TTL=2h. Use `/deploybot override unpin` to remove early.
leo: metrics I'm watching: cpu steal low, but memory high on a subset of nodes. attaching quick grep of logs below:
```
[kv-cache] evict loop: queue depth=1200
alloc::oom at kv slab grow
addr=0x7fe3f4e2
```
sasha: can we try a tiny kernel patch (revert the small alloc optimization) and rollforward? we can hotpatch on the canary nodes first. I can prepare a PR and cherry-pick.
tara: +1 for patch probe. timeline? we should hold unpin until we confirm patch impact. no full rollback yet unless errors exceed 5% or latency > SLO.
kevin: agree. set guardrails: if memory OOM-rate > 1.5% for 15m or 99th latency +200ms we rollback. who is oncall to trigger?
jamie: tara is oncall; tagging @tara. tara pls ack. also please update release notes with a short blurb if we pin — we don't want customers surprised.
tara: ack. monitoring play: dashboards `canary/runtime/kvcache` and alert `kvcache-oom-canary`. I'll keep an eye and post status every 15m. if stable after 30m post unpin suggestion.
leo: sample rollback/unpin commands for docs:
```
# remove pin early
/deploybot override unpin runtime runtime-3.2.1 --scope=canary-eu-west --reason="verified fix applied"
# force rollback (route traffic back immediately)
/deploybot rollback runtime runtime-3.1.x --scope=canary-eu-west --reason="ooms exceeded threshold"
```
sasha: PR created: `hotfix/revert-kv-alloc-opt` -> CI green. requesting staged rollforward to 5 canary nodes. I'll push patch in 10m.
kevin: good. can we also add a tiny telemetry probe producing sample dumps when eviction loop crosses threshold? helps for postmortem.
tara: added a temporary probe to the canary config. verbose logs for 30m.
deplybot: (system) deploy task scheduled: rollforward patch to 5 nodes at 4690123475, check health at 4690123495.
sasha: rolled to 5 nodes — initial look: memory trend flattening on 3 nodes, 2 still spiky. continuing.
tara: 15m check: OOM-rate down to 0.6% and 99p latency within SLO. recommending to keep pin for remainder of TTL, then unpin if stable 30m window holds.
kevin: sounds good. please add the following short release note snippet to the pinned runtime changelog: "Temporary pin of runtime-3.2.1 in eu-west canary due to kv-cache regression; hotfix applied and under observation."
jamie: also note ops-runbook link: https://docs.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-oom
deplybot: pin TTL expires at 4690124656. Will auto-unpin unless override.
tara: will update status and close thread after auto-unpin or manual unpin. thanks all. :thumbsup:
